law_name: Personal Data Protection and Privacy Act 2025
jurisdiction: Information Commission (designated National Data Protection Commission)
scope: Data subjects in The Gambia (extraterritorial: foreign controllers processing data of people in The Gambia)
applies_to: All public and private controllers and processors; excludes purely personal/household activity and anonymous data
key_requirements: Accountability-based compliance with no prior registration required; breach notification to the Commission within 72 hours (and to data subjects without undue delay if high risk); DPIA required for high-risk processing; DPO mandatory for public authorities and large-scale monitoring/sensitive-data processing
data_categories: Personal data; sensitive personal data (genetic and biometric data, racial origin, political opinions, health status), processing generally prohibited unless a specific condition applies
penalties_range: Administrative: corrective warnings, enforcement notices, processing bans and fines set by the Commission (reported GMD 1 million or 5% of gross income; 4% of global turnover for serious cases). Criminal: up to 3 years or fine from GMD 500,000 for unlawful processing for gain; up to 5 years for selling data (10 years and fines from GMD 10 million for corporations if aggravated); 2 years for concealing a breach; 7 years for obstructing the Commission
exemptions: Purely personal or household activity; anonymous data
research_exemption: Specific basis for processing for archiving in the public interest, scientific, historical or statistical purposes, subject to safeguards (section number not confirmed)
genetic_data: Special category (2024 Bill s. 3 definition); processing prohibited unless an exception with safeguards applies (s. 6); enacted 2025 numbering may differ
notes: Passed unanimously by National Assembly 29 September 2025; assent reported 7 November 2025 by secondary sources only; no commencement order or gazette found.
